content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In Christian teaching, 'shadow' most commonly symbolizes divine protection and refuge — being sheltered under God's presence, pictured as resting in the shadow of His wings or of the Almighty. God's shadow represents nearness, covering, and safety for those who trust Him.","primary_basis":["Psalm 91:1 (abiding under the shadow of the Almighty)","Psalm 17:8 (hide me under the shadow of your wings)","Psalm 36:7 (children of men take refuge in the shadow of your wings)","Psalm 57:1 (in the shadow of your wings I will take refuge)","Psalm 63:7 (in the shadow of your wings I sing for joy)","Psalm 121:5 (the LORD is your shade at your right hand)","Isaiah 25:4 (a shade from the heat, a refuge from the storm)","Isaiah 49:2 (in the shadow of his hand he hid me)","Song of Solomon 2:3 (I sat down under his shadow with great delight)"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Typological foreshadowing: Old Testament laws, rituals, and institutions as a 'shadow' of the reality (substance) found in Christ and heavenly things — the shadow-versus-substance contrast central to Christian typology.","basis":["Colossians 2:16-17 (these are a shadow of the things to come, but the substance belongs to Christ)","Hebrews 8:5 (a copy and shadow of the heavenly things)","Hebrews 10:1 (the law has but a shadow of the good things to come)"],"prominence":"dominant"},{"meaning":"Transience and brevity of human life: shadow as an image of fleeting, insubstantial existence.","basis":["Job 8:9 (our days on earth are a shadow)","Job 14:2 (he flees like a shadow and does not continue)","1 Chronicles 29:15 (our days on the earth are like a shadow)","Psalm 102:11 (my days are like an evening shadow)","Psalm 144:4 (his days are like a passing shadow)","Ecclesiastes 6:12 (life passed like a shadow)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Death, darkness, and gloom: 'the shadow of death' (tsalmavet) as an image of mortal danger, deep darkness, or spiritual gloom from which God delivers.","basis":["Psalm 23:4 (the valley of the shadow of death)","Isaiah 9:2 / Matthew 4:16 (those dwelling in the region and shadow of death, light has dawned)","Luke 1:79 (to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death)","Job 10:21-22 (the land of darkness and the shadow of death)"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Changeability and instability contrasted with God's immutability: God has 'no variation or shadow due to change,' making shadow a symbol of mutability and inconstancy.","basis":["James 1:17 (with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning)"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Conveyed divine power or presence through a person: shadow as a medium of healing or overshadowing power.","basis":["Acts 5:15 (Peter's shadow falling on the sick)","Luke 1:35 (the power of the Most High will overshadow you)"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"False or unreliable security: the shade of human alliances or rulers as inadequate protection compared with God's.","basis":["Isaiah 30:2-3 (seeking shelter in the shadow of Egypt shall be your humiliation)","Judges 9:15 (take refuge in the shade of the bramble)"],"prominence":"rare"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"medium","notes":"Shadow is a genuinely polyvalent biblical image with no single settled symbolic meaning; interpretation is context-dependent. Two meanings compete for primacy: (1) devotional/Old Testament usage strongly favors protection and refuge under God, and (2) doctrinal/New Testament usage strongly favors the typological shadow-versus-substance contrast (Colossians 2:17; Hebrews 8:5; 10:1), which is arguably the most distinctively Christian theological use of the term. Reference works such as the Dictionary of Biblical Imagery typically list protection, transience, and foreshadowing as parallel senses rather than ranking one as definitive. I have listed protection as primary because it is the most frequent scriptural usage, but the typological sense is at least equally prominent in Christian theological teaching, so it is marked dominant among the alternatives."}
